  • The code review (a DAW, Linux desktop and Home Assistant user, reviewing the code with counter-examples) found seven bugs no scenario had caught, all fixed with a test each: a held slot didn't reserve a channel it showed in auto, nor did pins check for one, so a channel could be on two slots; auto took a channel before the pool of channels meant for it; pool members had no delay (a Mumble reconnect moved a fader twice) and hold wasn't used; persist didn't apply to modes, and any mode edge ended a pick; replays missed flaps after long stable times. Also: present in a state's when is an error now, composed states have no delays of their own, simulate checks its options, and --table no longer shows composed states apart from what they name.

items.title: Decisions after the live test
items.text:
The prototype ran on the author's device (the example). Decided then:

  1. People only share auto (revised 2026-11-17 in people-slots.md: people, apps and auto are built-in pools). people is no candidate of a slot any more, and share goes: people always take auto slots from the right, in their order. One way to place people; no paging. Fixed people are person channels.
  2. Slots replace strips and layouts in the daemon. Not a translation into today's strips: channel controllers that live as long as the configuration, bound to slots by the resolver (The daemon).
  3. The conditions stay as they are ("x if y" strings with the grammar above): they read well and worked on the device.
  4. One format. The old one goes: no reading of it, and no migrate-config either (Migration). The GUI, the docs and init-config move to the new format.
  5. person channels without a slot join the people as themselves (in_pool to opt out), like apps channels join auto.
  6. Starting the voice chat is a control of the slot VoIP shows on: 7 = { select = { launch = [...] }, when = "not call" } in [controls]; the VoIP channel stays hidden outside a call, the strips of people have no launch.
  7. [people], not [pool.people]: people are no pool any more (revised 2026-11-17: [pool.people]).
  8. [controls]: actions that belong to a slot, whatever it shows (Controls). Options of places only look, or act on applications without a channel.

Found on the device and changed in the prototype: call on at once and off after 5 s (a delay showed VoIP and Mic after the people, a long one hid leaving); people in a learned order instead of fixed home slots (no empty slots); people from the right, applications from the left (they don't push each other around); voice_chat also alone (the mic before anyone comes); the meters of people on the dB scale like every other meter.

items.title: Migration
items.text:
Not built (decided 2026-11-17: a clean break). An old file fails check-config; this is how to write it anew:

Old New A strip A channel and a candidate in the slot of its position. Its id: its id; for a strip with Home Assistant entities strip_<position> (so select.xtouch_strip_1_output keeps working), with a suggestion to rename it; else its label in lower case, else <type>_<n>. homeassistant strips that share entities across layouts One channel. An auto strip auto; its options that differ from those of the other auto strips become options of the place. Candidates the same as the slot's fallback are dropped. A voip strip Without person: a people candidate, its look goes to [pool.people]; people fill slots from the right in their order, so their strips move; label and paging go. With person: a person channel. A launch goes to [controls] of its slot, select = { launch = ... } (decision 6). fader/encoder = "homeassistant" and launch of an auto strip [controls] of its slot, with id = "strip_<n>" so the entities keep their ids. An empty strip "-". A [[layout]] A [state.<name>] mode = true with its rules, label and priority; each of its strips a candidate if <name> above the default one of that slot. meter_point of a layout meter_point on the places of its candidates. An inherit strip A candidate of the channel it refers to. The report names every one it resolved, so surprises (like the one in the motivation) show. collapse on a strip The strip stays in its slot as "<id> if present" above auto: nothing shifts any more. The report lists them and points to pools of channels for those who want filling by order. behavior.auto_hold, behavior.ignore [pool.apps] hold, exclude. behavior.collapse_hold behavior.absent_after. switching.hold delay_off of each mode. switching.chord = [1, 8] chord = { strips = [1, 8], action = "cycle_modes" }. The remembered layout (layout_file) The kept override of the mode. Strips with the same strip_<n> entities in several layouts that control different things Separate channels; the report names the entities that are renamed. select.xtouch_layout, xtouch-daemon layout select.xtouch_mode, xtouch-daemon mode; the old command fails with a pointer, the report names the entity for automations.

No compatibility reading of the old format.

items.title: Sixth review (the integration of the fifth)
items.text: Finding Decision A pinned member a held slot shows went to its pin's slot too: one stream on two strips. A pin waits while a held slot shows its member. Claims could change under a finger; a release could go to another owner than the press. Held slots keep their claims; dispatch is sticky and routes by control. Minor: untyped pins and members by display name; an id on controls without Home Assistant; an empty launch; launch_when_running in [people]; LEDs of claimed buttons with a when; the chord check outside the model; two homes for Home Assistant faders; LEDs under claims. Step 4; errors; refused; one owner per LED; step 6; both stay, the slot's claim wins; stated. bind() lacked the meter point the Desk needs for its meters. bind(slot, presenter, meter_point). Owner: one table of controls per slot can't change with the mode (layouts with different controls on a strip). A list per slot, the first whose when holds. Owner: toggle:<mode> had no meaning (modes have no override of their own). Picks the mode, the next press back to auto.

items.title: Fifth review (the integration of the fourth, and actions of places)
items.text: Finding Decision Actions (a Home Assistant knob, a launch) only worked through what the slot showed: a channel or a person there silently disabled them. [controls] per slot (decision 8). Blocker: participant names and channel ids were one namespace of members: someone called browser became the Browser channel and broke the strips. Typed members (application, channel, person). Options that kept people off a place disagreed between code and design; place ids couldn't be reused; decision 6 hung on people skipping places. Gone with [controls]: only pins keep people out. Minor: launch in [people]; a [voip] provider in every configuration; auto present for people who never sit in it; a dropped pin kept people out; the table doesn't explore people; participant ids. Refused; said in the design (people share auto everywhere, the bridge socket costs nothing without a voice chat); fixed; fixed; Simulate gets a count of people (step 7); step 4. Doc: the Places row against the people rule, a fifth review that didn't exist, where [people] is edited, "then the people" as a pool. Fixed. Step 2 not concrete. Step 2.

items.title: Fourth review (architecture, after the live test)
items.text: Finding Decision Blocker: entities were named by strip (strip_<n>) and went away with a channel's slot; place options overrode a channel's controls and id. Entities per channel and place id, registered once per configuration; place ids in the namespace; place options only for applications without a channel. Blocker: the mixer handed out the applications of auto itself, in its own order, next to the resolver; pins never reached the resolver. The resolver alone; pick and pins are requests to the SlotEngine. Touch and held buttons died with each new mixer. The Desk lives as long as the daemon. People on places with controls, people and pins. People skip pinned slots and places with control options; pick only lists applications. The presence of auto didn't count people. It does. person channels without a slot vanished. They join the people (decision 5). Leftovers of share and the people candidate. Gone; [people]. A reload lost the run state. The SlotEngine outlives the configuration. Controllers had their place built in; the live view counted strips by layout. Look and identity when bound; a snapshot of slots and states. The voice chat's launch had no home. A launch on the place VoIP leaves (decision 6). Minor: clocks, people by name, sensor.xtouch_slot_<n>, migration rows, polling, entity churn of the prototype. loop.time(), ids for members, the sensor's format, the rows, deadlines; the native runtime ends the churn.

items.title: First review (DAW, Linux desktop and Home Assistant user)
items.text: Finding Decision voip was both a channel and the built-in pool. Pools became a concept; one namespace and the pool people. An off-delay without an on-delay: a notification sound turns call on for 30 s. delay_on/delay_off; recording and voice_chat as sources. "Leftmost wins" ranks by position. Rank first, ties to the left. Too many ways to say "when". One expression language; tags only group channels; when is exclusive with sources. Modes and states were two concepts with two syntaxes. mode = true on a state; every state has an override. present was undefined for absent channels. An absent channel holds (dark, keeps its place); if present skips it. A touchless fader can't protect "nothing under a finger". It counts as touched after the user moved it. No feedback when a slot swaps. The new label plus the reason. Home Assistant needs to know what shows where. sensor.xtouch_slot_<n>, binary_sensor.xtouch_<id>_shown. Long syntax. [channel.<id>], the compact slot form. GUI: preview and override looked the same; no overview. Read-only state bar with override menu, Simulate, chips, one inspector, the why line, the grid. Migration breaks strip_<n> entities. Kept where entities exist, with a rename suggestion.

items.title: Second review (DAW, Linux desktop, Home Assistant user, systems design)
items.text: Finding Decision Stickiness made the result depend on history. Channels go by rank, then position, without history; only members of auto and people keep their slots. Incumbency as a tie-breaker (proposed) would break the example the same way, so ties go to the leftmost slot. "Holds" and "shows" are separate terms. Pools: circular, no order, auto_hold missing, no per-place options or ids. See the third review for the final rules; hold; options for a place and id. launch unreachable behind a condition; the Mic's Rec indicator hidden. Pitfalls section and check-config warnings. Paging, person strips, pick, collapse_hold had no home. Paging of people; type = "person"; pick as today; absent_after. Overrides vs delays, persistence, mode select without auto, when ORed with sources, loops, the chord freezing slots. Overrides bypass delays; one persistence rule (third review); auto in the mode select; when exclusive; loops are errors; chord buttons don't hold slots. Expression language. Grammar; one namespace with reserved words; pools without a prefix; tags named after kinds; errors with positions. GUI: Simulate, grid explosion, why not, cards, overridden style. All adopted. Home Assistant: feeding states, the mode select, formats, attributes. homeassistant = true with an input switch; formats and attributes defined. Daemon: batching, dwell, startup, reload, polling, logging, voice_chat. All adopted. Migration notes, deliberately empty slots. Adopted; "-".

items.title: Third review (the same profile, with hand traces of the example)
items.text: Finding Decision Blocker: pools and fall-through were circular; the steps didn't say how they iterate. Pools always hold (like channels); if present with pool presence counted before assignment; conditions depend only on inputs; the steps run once each, in order. Blocker: an exhausted stack and a held slot were undefined; motor moves of touchless faders. An implicit trailing auto ("-" for dark); held and dwelling slots are fixed inputs whose channel is reserved; motor moves don't count. Blocker: the example's table showed a scene that barely exists (people present means call with Mumble) and slot 8 changed twice. The example asked people if gaming and present and dropped Browser from slot 8 (replaced after the live test: people share auto). Blocker: a hidden channel's streams in auto had two owners. auto hands out whatever plays and has no slot, hidden apps channels as a whole; in_auto = false opts out. Blocker: four contradictions (meter_point, buds as state and channel, switching.hold, the noisy slot 4). meter_point on channels and places; the state is wireless; switching.hold goes; slot 4 removed from the example. Options for a place leaked entity ownership; options of today's auto strips missing. Look options on any candidate; control options and id on pool candidates only; the missing ones added. Pools of channels: shown twice, priority inverted, collapse migration too broad, Select. Members exclude channels with a slot; pools of channels fill by order; collapse migrates to if present in place; Select pages only on people. Three persistence rules; startup as an edge. One rule; overrides are kept across restarts; startup is the baseline. Entity ID collisions; shared homeassistant strips in migration. Reserved ids; one channel for shared entities. pick changed meaning. As today. Coverage: chord syntax, mode --next, the CLI, person name overlap, ignore vs exclude, auto_hold, the live device in the GUI, Mumble outside its slots. All adopted. Minor: banner and flashes, chip text, the presets link, cycle order, why for channels. All adopted. Newcomer configuration and init-config. A new configuration.

items.title: Design: try changes and situations on the device
items.text: Status: built (2026-11-18), extended by the virtual twin, replaced by Previews, in the GUI or on the device (2026-11-19).

items.title: Problem
items.text:
The GUI has two ways to see a configuration before it is real, and they don't know each other:

  • Try on the device (the live preview, live.StartPreview): the daemon runs the unsaved configuration of the editor instead of the file. The device follows every edit, but only in the situation there is right now.
  • Simulate on the page Slots: what the slots would show in another situation (another mode, states on or off, channels absent, so many people in the call, applications that play, devices without a channel). The resolver computes it in the GUI, only the drawing shows it, and nothing can be played: no daemon runs those strips.

Both answer "what would the device do if ...": with this configuration, and in this situation. Trying a situation on the device itself (the real one, or the virtual one) is what Simulate can't do.

items.title: Idea
items.text:
One preview with two optional parts, both run by the daemon:

  • the configuration: the editor's (unsaved changes), or the file;
  • the situation: the what-if of Simulate, or the real one.

The switch "Try on the device" (next to Save and apply) sends whatever differs from reality: the unsaved changes, and while Simulate is open, its situation too. With the switch off, Simulate stays what it was before: the drawing only. So the real device never changes without that switch (decision 1).

items.title: The situation in the daemon
items.text:
StartPreview gets an optional situation (slots.outcomes.Situation: mode, on, flipped, people, apps, devices, as gui.domain.simulate.WhatIf), and its config may be None: the file's configuration, in that situation.

The SlotEngine runs a situation in a second Simulation of its own (what_if), next to the real one:

  • States and the mode are overrides and the mode picked of that Simulation: each state of the scene is forced on or off as the situation says, the mode is picked. The real overrides and the mode picked are not touched.
  • Presence and the members come from an Observation made for the situation (Situation.observation): for a present apps channel an application its match takes, for an output/input channel its devices, for a person channel that person in the call; absent ones get none. The pools get their stand-ins: apps applications, people people, devices devices. Stand-ins are taken from what is real first (applications that play now, people in the call, devices without a channel), then made up (App 3, Person 2, Device 1): a real one has audio behind its strip, a made-up one shows its label on a strip that controls nothing.
  • Delays and dwells apply as in reality: a state switched on in the situation waits its delay_on, a channel that goes absent stays absent_after seconds. That is the point of trying it on the device.
  • The real Simulation is not stepped while a situation runs, and nothing of the situation is kept: no slots.json, no people.json.

engine.active is the Simulation that runs (the situation's, or the real one); the SlotMixer and the live view use it (see Live view for the preview around it). Home Assistant keeps the real one: its slot sensors and state sensors are not updated while a situation runs, so automations never see a made-up situation. The live view tells simulated: true in the snapshot, with the slots and states of the situation.

What the device does on its own during a situation: the chord, Home Assistant's mode select and the overrides go to the real engine (they are real requests); the device shows the situation until it ends.

The situation ends with the preview: the switch off, Simulate ended (the configuration stays previewed if it has changes), the window closed or not answering for PREVIEW_TIMEOUT, the file changed. Then the real Simulation steps again at once and the slots show reality.

items.title: The GUI
items.text:
• Simulate with the switch on: the what-if goes to the daemon (debounced like edits), the drawing shows the live device (with the accent frame while the situation runs), the cards show the daemon's slots and their why, and Play works: the faders of real stand-ins move their audio.
  • Simulate with the switch off: as before, the resolver in the GUI, the drawing only, no Play. Its bar says "Only in the drawing: turn on Try on the device to run it on the device."
  • The switch is there while there are unsaved changes or Simulate is open, and a daemon can take it.
  • The pill next to it: "On the device, not saved", "On the device · simulated", "On the device, not saved · simulated", "Sending to the device…", "Paused: problems".
  • Esc ends Simulate as before; with the switch on the device goes back to the real situation.

items.title: Decisions (2026-11-18)
items.text:
1. Simulate drives the device only while "Try on the device" is on. Without it, nothing reaches the device.
  2. One preview in the daemon (configuration and situation), not a second mechanism: the same client, heartbeat, timeout, and ending.
  3. Stand-ins are real where they can be, made up otherwise.
  4. Home Assistant never sees a situation.

items.title: Not now
items.text:
• The chord and Home Assistant changing the situation instead of reality while one runs.
  • A banner on the device ("SIM") while a situation runs.

items.title: Design: the virtual twin
items.text: Status: built (2026-11-19), replaced by Previews, in the GUI or on the device (2026-11-19): one control shows edits and Simulate in the GUI (on the twin) or on the device. It added a twin to Try changes and situations, which stayed as it was, and replaced the drawing that the GUI made without a device (what it shows instead: A simulated device).

items.title: Problem
items.text:
The GUI draws the device. It has three sources for that drawing:

Source Where the strips come from The device, live The daemon's mirror of the device: every byte its Surface sent (Surface.mirror, live.server.strip_states). Simulate, no "Try on the device" gui/domain/simulate.py: the GUI runs the resolver and paints a label and a color. No daemon Was the same as Simulate: the file in its default situation (removed on 2026-11-19, the strips are dark now).

The second row is a second implementation of "what a strip looks like". It knows nothing of meters, rings, LEDs, faders, banners or the strip controllers, so it can only be wrong in new ways, and nothing can be played on it. The rule for the GUI is: the drawing is only ever the mirror of a device that the daemon drives. A device the user doesn't have is a virtual one, and the same holds for a situation the user doesn't have: it needs a device of its own that something drives.

items.title: Idea
items.text:
A virtual twin: a second, complete set of strips that the daemon runs for the situation of Simulate, next to the real ones. The situation keeps its second use: with "Try on the device" on, the real device shows it too, as before. The twin is what Simulate draws and plays on in every case. It is built from the same parts as the real device (Surface, Desk, SlotMixer, SlotEngine, the strip controllers) and touches nothing real. The GUI asks for it and draws its mirror, exactly like the mirror of the real device. Without a daemon there is no twin, so no drawing: the GUI guides to the daemon.

flowchart LR
    subgraph Daemon
        direction TB
        RS[Surface] --> RM[mirror]
        RE[SlotEngine] --> RX[SlotMixer / Desk] --> RS
        SS[sound server] --> RE
        TW[World of a Situation] --> TN[SlotEngine]
        TN --> TX[SlotMixer / Desk] --> TS[Surface, no port] --> TM[mirror]
    end
    RM -- "Snapshot: strips, slots" --> GUI
    TM -- "TwinView: strips, slots" --> GUI

The twin has no port: a Surface writes everything it sends into its mirror whether a device is connected or not (Surface.send()), which is how the real mirror shows "what the device will show once it is there". A spike on 2026-11-19 confirmed it: a Surface on a port that never opens still mirrors texts, LEDs and rings. The twin needs no SimulatedDevice socket or transport; the mirror is its device.

items.title: What "touches nothing real" means
items.text:
The twin is built from a Config and from nothing of the daemon: it gets no reference to the real backend, surface, bridge, voice chat provider, player list or state directory. That is the guarantee, not a check at each effect. What each part of the real path becomes:

Real Twin AudioBackend (the sound server) TwinBackend: holds an AudioState, set_* change that state and report it like the sound server does. AudioState Made from the situation and the real names (see The world). The real state is never passed on. VoipProvider (the plugin) DemoProvider (the provider of the demo mode): people from the situation, volume and mute stay in its memory. Meters (pw-record per target) A signal generator fed through the same Meter.feed_from(), scaled by the gain of the target. Launcher (launch) The Launcher with a spawn that does nothing (it takes one already). MQTT bridge, Home Assistant None: bridge=None. Home Assistant never sees the twin. Media players (encoder = "media") None, as without a player. state_dir (choices, people) None: no file is read or written. Processes (states processes = [...]) None run; states are forced by the situation (overrides, as now). Log The twin's engine logs at debug level under xtouch_daemon.twin. Hands (buttons, faders, encoders) Play events for the twin go to its own Surface.play().

items.title: The world of a situation
items.text:
A Situation (slots.outcomes: mode, on, flipped, people, apps, devices) is turned into an Observation for the real device by Situation.observation() (which stays, for "Try on the device"). The twin makes a whole world from it instead, and its engine goes through the normal path: Observer.observe(audio, processes, voip, now) is what a real step does.

world(scene, situation, names) -> World(audio: AudioState, voip: VoipState, processes: frozenset[str]), with names the applications that play and the people in the voice chat right now, as plain strings (see Decision 2):

Part of the scene In the world, unless the situation flipped it output / input channel One device per entry of its devices: the first (or the second, ...) as a made-up node with a description of its own (Device 1), a volume of 100 %. A channel with a wildcard gets one device that matches it. Without devices the default one. apps channel One playing stream whose name matches its first match entry (a preset: its first name). person channel The person in the voice chat. homeassistant channel Nothing: it is always present. apps pool situation.apps playing streams: the real applications first, then App 1, App 2, ... (the pool flipped: all slots). people pool situation.people people: the real ones first, then Alice, Bob, ... devices pool situation.devices devices: the real ones that no channel has first, then Device 1, ... Pools of channels Their channels are present as channels are; flipping the pool removes them all. Pools of applications and of people of your own flipped: one stand-in that the pool takes (its match, its people); absent otherwise.

Everything else (states, modes) is the situation's on and mode: overrides and a mode picked in the twin's SlotEngine, as the real preview does it now. Delays and dwells apply as in reality (delay_on, absent_after, hold): that is the point of a twin that runs.

items.title: Decision 2: the twin takes the real names, and nothing else
items.text:
The device that "Try on the device" drives shows real applications and people as stand-ins where it can (try-and-simulate decision 3), because it has audio behind them. The twin has no real audio behind anything, but it takes the same names first, so the twin and the device show the same words for the same situation. The daemon hands StartTwin's world the names as plain strings, copied; the twin holds no reference to the sound server, the voice chat or their state. Everything else in the world is made up.

The price: the strips of the twin depend on what plays right now, so the same configuration and situation give other strips at another time. Tests give the names.

items.title: The twin in the daemon
items.text:
runtime/twin.py. Each client's twin is made by the daemon with the current names, and gets new ones when they change (Twin.set_names()), so a stand-in follows what plays:

class Twin:
    """The strips of a configuration in a situation, on a device of their own."""

    def __init__(self, config: Config, situation: Situation): ...
    def set_situation(self, situation: Situation) -> None: ...  # a new world, same engine and strips
    def set_names(self, names: Names) -> None: ...  # the real applications and people changed
    def reconfigure(self, config: Config) -> None: ...  # like a reload: ids carry over
    def play(self, event: StripEvent) -> None: ...  # a hand on the twin
    def view(self) -> TwinView: ...  # strips of the mirror + slots, states, why
    async def run(self) -> None: ...  # the steps, the meters; cancelled by close()
    def close(self) -> None: ...

It owns a Surface(port=NoPort()), a Desk(surface, chord, on_chord, capturer=pulse), a SlotEngine(config, state_dir=None, logger=...), a SlotMixer(surface, TwinBackend, config, engine, desk, DemoProvider, bridge=None, players=None, launcher=Launcher(spawn=...)), and a task that steps the engine like the daemon does (wake on a change of the world, the deadline of a delay or a dwell, every PROCESS_INTERVAL). As built, these parts, the loop and the step are one class that both are (Rig, runtime/rig.py); the daemon adds the real processes and Home Assistant to the step (_processes(), _stepped()), the twin its world.

The twin's strips are lit by the first step: Surface writes every color and text into its mirror, connected or not.

items.title: Seams that the twin needs in the existing code
items.text: Where Change hardware/surface.py NoPort (a Port that is never there), hand(data) (bytes as if the device sent them). Nothing else: Surface already mirrors without a transport. audio/meter.py, runtime/desk.py Meter(..., capturer=...) and Desk(..., capturer=...): the function that feeds peaks of a target (Capturer, with the gain it is told). The default is capture() (a process); the twin's feeds a fixed, slowly changing pattern while the target plays. runtime/slots.py SlotEngine(..., logger=...). The situation (what_if, simulate(), active) stays: it is the real device's. slots/outcomes.py, slots/world.py Situation.observation() stays for the real device; slots/world.py is new (the twin's world). simulate() and outcomes() stay: check-config and the table of Simulate's inputs use them. voip/ DemoProvider.set_people(names): the people of the world, volume and mute of those who stay are kept. runtime/daemon.py Twins by client, fed with the real names. preview() and snapshot().simulated stay. live/messages.py, codec.py, server.py See The protocol.

items.title: The protocol
items.text:
The snapshot is one line for every client. A twin belongs to one client, so its view is its own line, sent to its owner only.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StartTwin:
    """Run `config` (the whole TOML text) in `situation` on a twin of your own; again: the twin follows."""

    config: str
    situation: Situation


class KeepTwin: ...  # the heartbeat, as KeepPreview


class EndTwin: ...  # the twin is gone


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Play:  # gets `twin: bool = False`: the hand is on the twin
    event: StripEvent
    twin: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TwinView:
    config: str  # fingerprint(config) of the twin, as Snapshot.config
    strips: tuple[StripState, ...]
    slots: SlotsState  # slots, states, mode, why and who waits: the twin's
  • Replies: Reply("twin", ok, message) to StartTwin (the errors of the configuration as in "preview"), Reply("twin_ended", True, why) when the daemon ended it (heartbeat missed, the daemon stops).
  • The view line is {"twin": {...}}, sent by LiveServer.tell_view(client, view) whenever it changes (at first every INTERVAL; pushed since 2026-11-19) (meters and motors keep it changing, like the snapshot).
  • Feature twin in FEATURES, next to situation, which stays. An older daemon lacks twin: Simulate says it is too old and to restart it. Nothing else of the protocol changes.
  • One twin per connection. A twin ends with EndTwin, with its connection, and after TWIN_TIMEOUT (10 s) without KeepTwin.
  • Security: as StartPreview, only the user's own clients (peer_uid). The configuration text may hold secrets ([mqtt]); the twin ignores [mqtt] and [voip] providers (it builds a DemoProvider, never a socket).

items.title: The twin's own hands
items.text: A button, fader or encoder on the twin (Play, the mouse on its drawing) goes through its own Desk and changes the twin's AudioState through TwinBackend, and a pick encoder what a slot of auto shows. The mode and the states are the GUI's alone: the chord, a toggle: or mode: control and requests of modes and overrides change nothing on the twin (SlotEngine.fixed), so the bar of Simulate and the twin never disagree. (Planned first: the twin changes them and the GUI follows; dropped, two owners of the what-if.)

items.title: The GUI
items.text:
• Simulate needs a daemon of this user that takes twin. Without one the page says why in its place (like "Try on the device" does, unavailable()), with the same guidance: start the daemon, or "Try without a device". There is no Simulate without a daemon.
  • It needs no "Try on the device", and no daemon that runs this file: the configuration it sends is the document's, so Simulate works on a new file, or on a daemon that reads another one.
  • While Simulate is open the GUI sends StartTwin(document.render(), situation) a moment after each edit or click (DEBOUNCE_MS) and KeepTwin every HEARTBEAT_MS; a document with problems sends nothing (the twin keeps the last one that parsed, the problems show as they do).
  • The drawing shows the TwinView strips while Simulate is open, with the accent frame ("simulated"), and the real mirror otherwise. Between the request and the first view the drawing keeps what it had.
  • The cards (what a slot shows, why, who waits) are the twin's SlotsState. gui/domain/simulate.py shrinks to WhatIf (a value the user edits), Inputs (what a what-if can change) and presence_text; simulated() and simulated_faces() are deleted.
  • Play on the drawing sends Play(event, twin=True) while Simulate is open: the faders and buttons of the twin, never the real device.
  • "Try on the device" (the switch) is as it is: the unsaved configuration, and while Simulate is open its situation, on the real device. The twin runs either way.
  • Esc ends Simulate: EndTwin.

items.title: Decisions (2026-11-19)
items.text:
1. Simulate still reaches the real device with "Try on the device" (try-and-simulate decision 1 stands). The twin is added; it replaces only the drawing that the GUI made itself.
  2. The twin takes the real names, and nothing else (see Decision 2).
  3. One twin per client, no limit in the daemon.
  4. Simulate needs a daemon: no daemon, no twin, no drawing, only the guidance.

items.title: Implementation order
items.text:
1. Seams: NoPort, hand(), Meter/Desk capture, SlotEngine logger, Rig (runtime/rig.py).
  2. slots/world.py and TwinBackend, DemoProvider; Twin, unit-tested without a daemon: a twin of the example configuration shows its slots; the real backend of the daemon is never called.
  3. Protocol: messages, codec, LiveServer.tell_view, the daemon's twins.
  4. GUI: Simulate on the twin, the drawing, the cards, Play; delete simulated() / simulated_faces().
  5. Docs: the GUI guide (Simulate), try-and-simulate (marked as replaced in part), architecture (live view), changelog.

items.title: Tests
items.text:
• World: each row of the table, for the example configuration and for pools of your own.
  • Inertness: a daemon with spies for the backend, the voice chat provider, the bridge and the launcher. A twin with a situation, Play on its strips (volume, mute, launch), a reconfigure: none of the spies is called, and the real strips and the real SlotsState are unchanged.
  • Names: the same situation and names give the same TwinView strips (the meter pattern is a function of time since the start; tests set it); new names reach the stand-ins.
  • Protocol: codec round trips; a second client does not get the first one's view; the heartbeat; the end with the connection.
  • GUI: Simulate with a fake live daemon: sends StartTwin, draws its view, shows the cards of the view, Play sends twin=True; without a daemon the page guides and the drawing is dark.

items.title: First steps
items.text: Set up the device, test it, write a configuration and run the daemon as a service. No device at hand? See Without a device.

items.title: Set up the device
items.text:
The extender has to be in MC (Mackie Control) mode on USB. Out of the box it may be set to the network interface: then it shows IP: 192.168.001.100 wait... and ignores USB.

  1. Switch it off.
  2. Hold the Select button of strip 1 and switch it on: the setup menu opens.
  3. Set Mode to MC and Interface to USB with the encoders.
  4. Leave the menu (Select of strip 1 again, or switch it off and on).

Connect it over USB. It needs no driver. Your user needs access to its MIDI device in /dev/snd: desktop sessions grant it to the logged-in user. Without a session, add the user to the audio group. See Hardware for details.

items.title: Test the device
items.text:
xtouch-daemon test

Every strip lights its LCD in a color, its LEDs, ring and meter, and moves its fader. Afterwards the command shows what you do on the device: faders, buttons and encoders. Ctrl+C stops it.

Only one program can use the device. If the daemon already runs as a service, stop it before the test (systemctl --user stop xtouch-daemon), and close DAWs that use the device. Without a device, start the virtual one in another terminal (xtouch-daemon virtual-device) and run xtouch-daemon test --virtual-device; see Without a device.

items.title: Write a configuration
items.text:
A configuration names channels (what a strip can control), states (in a call, gaming) and, for each of the 8 slots, what its strip shows when. Concepts explains these words. Without a file the daemon uses the example configuration: the default input on slot 7, the default output on slot 8, and auto (the next application that plays) on the others. To make it yours, the easiest way is the GUI (xtouch-daemon-gui or xtouch-daemon gui): it shows the device live, every option with its help, and what a change does (Simulate); its "Save and apply" writes the file and loads it into the running daemon.

Setup tour builds a whole configuration that way, step by step, with the file it writes.

By hand, write the example to ~/.config/xtouch-daemon/config.toml and edit it:

xtouch-daemon init-config                 # writes ~/.config/xtouch-daemon/config.toml
xtouch-daemon list-devices [--snippet]    # the names to use for device channels (--snippet: channels to paste)
xtouch-daemon list-apps                   # the applications that play now, and which channel or slot takes them
xtouch-daemon check-config                # validates the file (with the line of each error) and shows what each slot shows when

For example, Bluetooth headphones on slot 1 while they are connected, and VoIP on slot 2 during a call:

[channel.buds]
type = "output"
device = "bluez_output.*"   # any Bluetooth headphones (their name holds an address; list-devices shows it)
label = "Buds"
color = "green"

[channel.voip]
type = "apps"
match = ["@voip"]   # Discord, Mumble, TeamSpeak and more, see Presets
label = "VoIP"

[state.call]
voice_chat = true   # in a channel of Mumble (with the plugin)

[slots]
1 = ["buds if present", "auto"]
2 = ["voip if call", "auto"]
# slots 3 to 8 have no entry: "auto", the next application that plays

check-config shows what this file does, as a table:

when               1     2     3-8
default            buds  auto  auto
call               buds  voip  auto
buds absent        auto  auto  auto
call, buds absent  auto  voip  auto

A row for each situation the slots ask about (call, whether buds is there) that changes something.

Channels, states and slots explains the format, Configuration every option.

items.title: Run it as a service
items.text:
xtouch-daemon install-service --now

This writes the systemd user unit ~/.config/systemd/user/xtouch-daemon.service, enables it and starts it. From now on it starts with your session. Without --now it only writes the unit.

The Arch Linux package has its own unit, so with it the command writes nothing: it enables and starts the unit of the package. The same without the command:

systemctl --user enable --now xtouch-daemon

A unit in ~/.config/systemd/user overrides the one of the package; see install-service.

Task Command Apply a changed configuration Nothing: the daemon takes the saved file. By hand: systemctl --user reload xtouch-daemon Restart (after changing [mqtt]) systemctl --user restart xtouch-daemon Stop (e.g. for xtouch-daemon test) systemctl --user stop xtouch-daemon See whether the device, sound server and broker are connected systemctl --user status xtouch-daemon Follow the log journalctl --user -u xtouch-daemon -f

To run it in the foreground instead, e.g. to watch the log while you try something:

xtouch-daemon run -l debug

Next: the Setup tour, then Concepts.

items.title: Arch Linux
items.text:
The AUR has two packages, built from the releases:

Package Contents xtouch-daemon-bin The daemon with its own Python 3.14 in /usr/lib/xtouch-daemon, the command xtouch-daemon, the systemd user unit /usr/lib/systemd/user/xtouch-daemon.service and the example configuration /usr/share/xtouch-daemon/config.example.toml. xtouch-daemon-gui-bin The GUI, xtouch-daemon-gui, with a menu entry. It runs on the system's Python and PyQt6, and needs xtouch-daemon-bin of the same version.

Install them with an AUR helper, e.g.:

paru -S xtouch-daemon-bin xtouch-daemon-gui-bin

Then enable the service, see Run it as a service. After an upgrade, restart it (systemctl --user restart xtouch-daemon): it runs the old version until then.

items.title: From the source
items.text:
xtouch-daemon uses haad-mqtt-autodiscovery from a checkout next to its own. Clone both side by side and install with uv:

git clone https://github.com/markusressel/xtouch-daemon
git clone https://github.com/haad-org/haad-mqtt-autodiscovery
uv tool install ./xtouch-daemon

uv installs Python 3.14 if your system does not have it. The command xtouch-daemon is then on your PATH.

For the GUI, install the gui extra instead. It brings Qt along, so it needs no system packages:

uv tool install --force './xtouch-daemon[gui]'

items.title: The GUI
items.text:
The GUI comes with xtouch-daemon-gui-bin (Arch Linux) or the gui extra (from the source), see above. It starts with xtouch-daemon-gui (the package, also "X-Touch Extender" in the menu of the desktop) or xtouch-daemon gui (from the source):

xtouch-daemon-gui            # the default configuration file
xtouch-daemon-gui -c FILE    # another one

Without the extra, xtouch-daemon gui says how to install it.

Next: First steps, then the Setup tour.

items.title: Setup tour
items.text:
One configuration, built step by step: the one the author runs. Every step says what to click in the GUI and what it writes to the file; use either, they edit the same file.

The goal, for the 8 strips (slots) of the device:

Slot Shows 1 The main output, with Select switching between phones, speakers and Bluetooth headphones. 2, 3 Slot 2 the browser and slot 3 the game, each while it plays; otherwise the next application that plays, otherwise a person of the voice chat. 4 to 6 People of the voice chat (from the right), otherwise applications. 7, 8 VoIP (7) and the microphone (8) while you are in a call; otherwise applications.

You need the daemon installed and the device set up and tested. The GUI starts with xtouch-daemon gui; without a configuration file it edits a new one and writes it with the first "Save and apply". That new file is empty: every slot shows auto, the next application that plays. The drawing of the device at the top shows what the file shows, as you edit. No device? Run the virtual one and use that one as the device in this tour.

items.title: 1. See what you have
items.text:
xtouch-daemon list-devices    # outputs and inputs: the names to use as `device`
xtouch-daemon list-apps       # what plays now, and which preset (@browsers, @games, ...) it belongs to

The GUI offers the same lists wherever a field asks for a device or an application (a click into the field opens them). Play something in the browser first, so that list-apps has an application to show.

items.title: 2. The main output
items.text:
GUI: page Channels, Add, Output from the sound server, pick your speakers. Rename the id to main_output (field next to the title; the slots that name it follow), set the label to Main (up to 7 characters: that is all the LCD has) and the color to cyan.

Select should switch between several devices, so add Choices: one per device, each with a label. A device that only exists in another profile of the sound card (the digital output, say) also needs the card and profile: list-devices prints both. Bluetooth headphones are best matched by a wildcard, because their name holds their address (bluez_output.*; list-devices --snippet writes it for you):

[channel.main_output]
type = "output"
color = "cyan"
label = "Main"

[[channel.main_output.choices]]
label = "Phones"
device = "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.analog-stereo"
card = "alsa_card.pci-0000_11_00.4"
profile = "output:analog-stereo+input:analog-stereo"

[[channel.main_output.choices]]
label = "Speaker"
device = "alsa_output.pci-0000_11_00.4.iec958-stereo"
card = "alsa_card.pci-0000_11_00.4"
profile = "output:iec958-stereo+input:analog-stereo"   # keeps the microphone (analog input) alive
max_volume = 200

[[channel.main_output.choices]]
label = "Buds"
device = "bluez_output.*"

See Devices for every option of choices.

items.title: 3. Applications
items.text:
GUI: Add, Applications. An apps channel is a group of applications that gets one strip: match names them (by a part of their name or program) or uses a preset such as @browsers, @voip or @games, which come with the daemon (Presets).

[channel.browser]
type = "apps"
match = ["@browsers"]
label = "Browser"
color = "blue"
meter = true

[channel.game]
type = "apps"
match = ["@games"]
label = "Game"

[channel.voip]
type = "apps"
match = ["@voip"]
label = "VoIP"
color = "yellow"
lit_when_idle = true        # the LCD stays lit while nothing plays: it is where the voice chat goes

items.title: 4. The microphone
items.text:
GUI: page Channels, Add, Input from the sound server, pick the microphone, then give it the label and the color.

[channel.mic]
type = "input"
device = "alsa_input.pci-0000_11_00.4.analog-stereo"
label = "Mic"
color = "red"
encoder = "balance"

items.title: 5. A state: in a call
items.text:
A state is when something matters. VoIP and the microphone should only take a strip while you are in a call, so make that a state. GUI: page States, Add, In a call (state); its sources are "You are in the voice chat" (Mumble, with its plugin) and "An application records" (Discord and the like have the microphone open while you talk):

[state.call]
voice_chat = true
recording = ["@voip"]
delay_off = 5               # stays on 5 s after the last source went off: a reconnect is not the end of the call

items.title: 6. The slots
items.text:
GUI: page Slots. Each slot is a card with its candidates, the first whose condition holds is shown. + adds a candidate at the end; pick one and the inspector sets what it shows ("Shows") and when ("When": empty is always, or a condition such as call, present, call and not gaming). Pick a slot's first candidate before adding the next: an empty slot is auto, so the first + shows it as a candidate you can change.

[slots]
1 = "main_output"
# the browser and the game while they play, else the next application, else a person
2 = ["browser if present", "apps", "people"]
3 = ["game if present", "apps", "people"]
# people from the right (6, 5, 4), else applications
4 = ["people", "apps"]
5 = ["people", "apps"]
6 = ["people", "apps"]
# VoIP and the microphone in a call, else applications
7 = ["voip if call", "apps"]
8 = ["mic if call", "apps"]
  • apps is the next application that plays and has no channel; people the next person of the voice chat; auto is both. A candidate that has nothing to show hands the slot to the one below it.
  • present means the candidate's own channel has something to control: the browser is playing.
  • Anything you leave out is auto.

items.title: 7. Settings of the whole daemon
items.text:
GUI: page Settings. The author lowers the volume a push on an encoder resets to, and renames an application that calls itself something unreadable:

[behavior]
reset_volume = 35

[aliases]
"WEBRTC VoiceEngine" = "Discord"

Three more settings finish the file. On Settings, Extender, the author picks the startup sequence show and switches fader 1 to touchless_faders, because its touch sensor is broken and the fader jumps back after every move (Behavior). On Channels, in the built-in pool People, the strips of people light up yellow:

[device]
touchless_faders = [1]
startup = "show"

[pool.people]
color = "yellow"

items.title: 8. Check it, then apply it
items.text:
xtouch-daemon check-config     # errors with the line they are in, then what every slot shows when

A long table shows the situations that change one thing; check-config --all has every combination.

The GUI shows the same on the page Slots: Simulate puts the device in another situation (in a call, nothing playing, a game running) and the drawing shows what the strips would show, on a virtual twin of the device in the daemon (so Simulate needs the running daemon), or on the device itself with the preview "On the device".

Save and apply writes the file. A running daemon takes it at once; otherwise the button next to the service at the top right ("Install and start") starts it as a systemd user service, so it is there from your next login on.
